previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with a chief complaint of burning epigastric pain radiating to the mouth, associated with a bitter taste and mild shortness of breath. Given his history of peptic ulcer disease, GERD, and cardiac risk factors, he was admitted to rule out myocardial infarction. Initial evaluation showed no ischemic changes on EKG, normal cardiac enzymes, and symptom improvement with omeprazole and a GI cocktail. The pain was determined to be due to gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). He remained hemodynamically stable, with resolution of symptoms during the stay. Chronic conditions including hypertension, aortic stenosis, chronic hyponatremia, and bronchitis were monitored and managed without intervention. He was discharged home with service, on optimized GERD therapy including omeprazole, with plans for H. pylori breath testing and follow-up with his gastroenterologist.

Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with a history of chronic

# Hyponatremia: The patient has a history of chronic 
hyponatremia secondary to SIADH. His baseline ranges from

symptomatic.  He was placed on a 1.5 L water restriction and 
started on salt tabs and his Na rose slowly.  By discharge his 
Na had increased to 129. TSH and cortisol WNL. His CT head and 
chest X-ray were unrevealing. He appeared euvolemic.  He had a 
fall within the last month so pain may have triggered his 
hyponatremia by increasing his ADH.  His pain was controlled 
with standing tylenol and tramadol prn as below.  He was 
discharged with a continued fluid restriction of 1500 cc/day, 
salt tabs 2 gm po TID.

# SOB: The patient has a history of chronic bronchitis and had 
subjective SOB on admission to the ICU. During his hospital 
admission he was sating well on room air.  He remained afebrile 
and his CXR was clear.  He was continued on fluticasone inhal 
bid and given albuterol and atrovent nebs prn.

# Bilateral UE pain: The patient had a recent fall and was 
admitted from rehab. He has known rotator cuff injuries. No 
fractures by report from survey performed at ___ 
___ after fall the fall.  His pain was controlled with 
Tylenol 1 gm TID standing, ultram prn, and lidocaine patches.
 
# HTN: The patient was initally continued on his outpatient 
regimen of metoprolol, isosorbide mononitrate, and valsartan.  
His SBP were noted to be persistent elevated so his valsartan 
was increased from 100 mg daily to 160 mg daily. 
 
# Chronic diastolic CHF: The patient remained euvolemic during 
his hospitalization.  He was continued on valsartan and 
metoprolol.  
  
# ? CAD: The paatient carries a history of CAD for unclear 
reasons as he has never had a positive stress test nor cardiac 
catheterization, has no WMA on ECHO and has no QWs on ECG.  He 
was continued on his outpatient medications including plavix, a 
statin, beta-blocker, and imdur.  
 
# PUD:  The patient has a history of H pylori. Unclear if he was 
treated.  He is scheduled for a breath test as an outpatient.  
He was continued on his PPI bid, ranitidine, and maalox prn.  
 
# Anemia: The patient was anemia, but remained within his 
basline Hct of ___ during his hospitalization.  On discharge 
his Hct was stable at 28.6. He had no clinical evidence of 
bleeding. Iron studies, B12, folate were normal when last 
checked in ___.  

# Rash/Itching: Per the son's report, the patient has a 
significant eczema history and uses moisturizing cream BID. 
While here he complained of itching. A recent derm note 
recommended hydroxyzine prn so he was started on this and was 
continued on his home creams and moisturizers.  
 
# Mouth pain: The patient reports that he has stomatitis and 
mouth pain.  He was started on Gelclair 15 mL tid with some 
relief.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital after a fall and found to have 
hyponatremia (low sodium).  You were monitored in the ICU 
initally.  You were placed on a fluid restriction of 1.5L per 
day which you should continue to follow as an outpatient.  You 
were also started on a salt tablet.

Changes to your medications:
1.  You should take 2 gm of salt three times daily.  
2.  Your valsartan was increased to 160 mg daily for better 
control of your blood pressure.    
3.  You can take gelclair 15 ML three times daily as need for 
mouth pain.  
4.  You can take hydroxyzine 25 mg every 6 hours as needed for 
itching.
5.  You should take tramadol 50 mg q4h prn for pain as needed.  
You should also take 1000 mg of tylenol three times daily for 
pain.
6.  You can take 15 mL of lactulose as needed for constipation.

Otherwise continue your outpatient medications as prescribed.

Go to the emergency room or call your primary doctor if you 
experience fevers, chills, confusion, another fall, chest pain, 
blood in your stool, or black stool.
